clue.text: He used 5 to see how people measured up

definitions.text: He used 5 to see how people measured up

parts.words: He used 5 to see how people measured up
parts.note: 5 down's answer is a bed; the clue pictures a figure of Greek myth who stretched or lopped his guests to fit his bed, so it was his gauge of how they measured up

explanation.surface: Someone running trials on equipment to assess people's stature.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference turns the bed of 5 down into a measuring device: in Greek myth this robber made every guest fit his bed exactly, by stretching or by cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical bandit of Attica forced travellers to fit his bed, making it a grim yardstick of their height.

clue.text: Artist about to put on his black

parts.note: re means about, concerning
noir is French for black, his own language's word for the colour

explanation.surface: A painter is about to don his dark clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' signals French, the painter's own language; 'to put on' sets the 'about' word in front of the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The French Impressionist painted scenes such as the Moulin de la Galette.

clue.text: Better college outside West African city

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo

indicators.note: the college name goes outside the letter for west

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school, formally Eton College

explanation.surface: A superior college beyond the western part of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West African' looks like one phrase but 'West' gives W, which 'outside' places inside ETON.
explanation.definitionFit: The South African coastal metropolis is that country's legislative capital.

clue.text: As would-be actor, risk failing test?

definitions.text: As would-be actor, risk failing test?

parts.words: As would-be actor, risk failing test?
parts.note: a stand-in performer for a lead role, punningly also someone who has not revised enough and so might fail an exam

explanation.surface: An aspiring actor who might flunk an audition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in who learns a role in case the principal cannot perform is a would-be actor.

clue.text: Equipment for checking engines in international base

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket or rugby match
a bed is a base or foundation

explanation.surface: Engine diagnostics equipment kept at a multinational base.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket and rugby a Test is a match between national teams.
explanation.definitionFit: A rig on which engines or machines are run for trials is a piece of checking apparatus.

clue.text: Observed new cut

parts.note: saw means observed

explanation.surface: Someone watched a fresh cut being made.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber that has been sliced with a toothed blade has been cut.

clue.text: Painting equipment that goes to Cockney's head?

parts.note: a grooming tool that goes to the head, said the Cockney way with the opening aitch dropped

explanation.surface: A painting tool that one Londoner uses on their hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, traditionally drop initial H sounds, so the tool for the hair becomes the painter's spray device.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine spray gun used by artists and retouchers is a piece of painting kit.

clue.text: This president liked, at heart, to be informal

definitions.text: This president liked, at heart, to be informal

parts.words: This president liked, at heart, to be informal
parts.note: the heart of the word liked holds the American leader's nickname, the informal form he went by

explanation.surface: A head of state who privately preferred casual manners.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of 'liked' is IKE, the famous nickname of the 34th US president ('I like Ike' was his slogan).
explanation.definitionFit: The Second World War general became the 34th President of the United States.

clue.text: Fool is going to island in place of saint

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person

explanation.surface: A clown heads off to an island to stand in for a holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian hill town is the home of St Francis, so it is a saint's place.

clue.text: Wearing a suit? Not half

definitions.meaning: in a card game, holding or playing in one of the four suits, here the black pointed one
British slang for 'very much so', 'in abundance'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is British understatement meaning 'and how!', the same as having something in large quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both 'in the suit of spades' and, idiomatically, 'in great abundance'.

clue.text: Bleating about having chance to get in touch

definitions.text: having chance to get in touch

indicators.note: the letters of the bleating word are moved about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A complaining person who whines on until given an opportunity to make contact.
explanation.definitionFit: Something palpable is capable of being felt, so it stands a chance of being touched.

clue.text: Exuberance in life, right?

indicators.note: the right letter sits inside the word for life

parts.note: bio is short for biography, a life story

explanation.surface: Asking whether high spirits are the correct way to live.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vivacity and dash, a lively exuberance of manner.

clue.text: Copper has nerve to take on athlete

indicators.note: the nerve word takes on the athlete in front of it

parts.note: a Blue is a sportsman who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University
bottle is British slang for courage or nerve

explanation.surface: A policeman shows the nerve to tackle a sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'Blue' is an Oxbridge sporting honour; 'bottle' is British slang for nerve. 'Copper' is old slang for a policeman, also once called a bluebottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebottle is dated British slang for a policeman, from the blue uniform.

clue.text: Sheer — ought to be changed?

parts.note: a playful hint that a garment one can view the body through is indecent and should be swapped for something else

explanation.surface: A gauzy outfit that its wearer really ought to replace.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer fabric is fine and transparent, letting light and the eye pass.

clue.text: Take lead, say, in this sort of band

definitions.meaning: lead is an example of a dense, toxic metallic element
a loud rock group playing a heavily amplified style

explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' is a link word: take lead as an example and you have the class it belongs to.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a dense metal of the toxic class, and the phrase also names a loud rock genre.

clue.text: Element briefly becoming socially acceptable

parts.note: the element's chemical symbol in short form is the single letter U, which is also the British label for upper-class, socially acceptable usage

explanation.surface: A substance that has quickly gained respectability in society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U' and 'non-U' were 1950s British terms for upper-class and not-quite-proper speech and habits; the element's symbol is the same letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This radioactive metal is a chemical element, atomic number 92.

clue.text: Desertion of a place of duty, say — terrible

parts.note: a post is where a sentry or soldier is stationed on duty

indicators.note: the word say is put through a terrible mangling of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone abandons their station, and that is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges SAY into ASY. 'say' looks like a link word but is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Renouncing one's faith or party is a desertion of a cause.

clue.text: Catcall about that dreadful bookmaker

indicators.note: the cat's cry goes around the other letters

parts.note: a mew is the call a cat makes

indicators.note: the word that is treated dreadfully, so its letters are mangled

explanation.surface: Someone heckles a terrible turf accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' scrambles the clue's 'that'. 'Bookmaker' looks like a betting man but means the writer of a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The evangelist wrote the first Gospel, so he made a book of the New Testament.

clue.text: Mouth quiet — it's ordered for him

parts.note: trap is slang for mouth, as in 'shut your trap'
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

indicators.note: the letters of it's are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Keep your mouth shut, the silent monastic order requires it of him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges IT'S into IST, and also hints at a religious order, whose monks keep strict silence.
explanation.definitionFit: A monk of the Cistercian order known for silence is the man the surface refers to.

clue.text: Runs out of sitting rooms? That's dangerous

indicators.note: the runs letter goes out of the word for sitting rooms

parts.note: parlours are sitting rooms
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Running out of lounges would be a perilous situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A precarious, perilous situation is a dangerous one.

clue.text: It takes more than vodka to get Red Army drunk

parts.note: bloody means blood-coloured, red

indicators.note: the army word is reeling about drunk, so its letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: Soldiers of the Soviet forces need plenty of spirits to get them intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges the army word. 'Red Army' reads as one phrase but splits into its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The cocktail combines vodka with tomato juice and seasoning, so it needs more than the spirit alone.

clue.text: Just opened, providing a drink

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a drink, usually of beer

explanation.surface: A door is barely open on condition that a beverage is offered.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'a jar' is an informal word for a glass of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left slightly open is said to be in that state.

clue.text: A person of distinction, moreover

parts.note: a swell is a fashionable, distinguished person

explanation.surface: A notable figure, and also something more.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means also or in addition, like 'besides'.

clue.text: Unfortunately out in test for 26

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit within the test word

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: the word out comes unluckily jumbled

explanation.surface: A batsman is unluckily dismissed in a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' scrambles the clue's 'out', and 'in' puts that inside the test word. 26 across is LESSON; the cricket picture of being out in a Test is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaching session with a tutor is a kind of class or instruction period.

clue.text: No-one cast up on a Scottish island

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are thrown upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: the word no plus I for one, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Nobody is washed up on a Hebridean isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No-one' splits into NO and ONE, with one as Roman I; 'cast up' turns that pair round, and 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The small Inner Hebridean isle is famed for St Columba's abbey.

clue.text: Frequently ring London papers

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
the Financial Times, abbreviated FT, and The Times are both London newspapers
the Financial Times, abbreviated FT, and The Times are both London newspapers

explanation.surface: Someone often phones the capital's newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adverb means often, on many occasions.

clue.text: Not so much performing as teaching

parts.note: less means a smaller amount
on describes someone on stage, performing

explanation.surface: Comparing how little time is spent acting with time spent instructing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun: 'teaching' as in a teaching or instruction given.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of instruction is a period of education given to pupils.

clue.text: Bull easy to shift? Yes, indeed!

indicators.note: the clue words are made to shift position, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking if a bull is easily moved and getting an emphatic yes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an emphatic affirmative, equivalent to 'certainly'.
